chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Sahhaf, from Al-Mundhir al-Jawwaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Those who fix (predict) the time have lied. Neither have we fixed a time for it in the past, nor would we do so in the future.

key_terms.الْمُوقِتُونَ: Those who fix or predict a specific time
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: The future / what is to come

ai.seo_question: What did the Imams say about those who predict the time of the Mahdi's reappearance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) refutes the 'Mawqitun' (those who fix times) by clarifying that the Imams neither revealed a specific fixed time in the past nor will they in the future, preserving the element of divine surprise. This distinction is crucial in Shia eschatology, differentiating between the general signs of the reappearance and the exact, unknown moment, which remains with Allah alone. The narration underscores the continuity of the Imam's authority during the Minor and Major Gheebah, where the timing remains hidden to test the faith of the believers.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 412 - Fadhl bin Shazan has narrated from Husain bin Yazid Sahaf from Mudhir Jawwaz from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:
“One who fixes (predicts) the time of the reappearance, has lied. Neither have we fixed a time for it in the past nor would we do so in future.”
